items.title: The rm guard denies unrelated deletions and misses the real one
acceptance: The guard evaluates only the shell segment containing the rm, so a store name in a later && ; or | segment does not deny it
The four reproduced false positives are covered by tests that fail against the current pattern
The true positives keep denying: bare store name, nested path, and the glob spellings the current comment names
Where the guard cannot see a deletion at all (an interpreter one-liner, fd -X rm), that limit is stated in the module comment rather than implied away
items.description: src/hooks.ts:240. The pattern is rm -r followed by [^\n]* followed by the store name, and [^\n]* crosses && ; and | freely. So any rm -r on a line that later mentions the store in ANY position is denied: a commit message, an --evidence flag value, a grep argument. Meanwhile the same deletion one indirection away is allowed. Reproduced against the shipped regex: 4 false positives, 2 bypasses. The practical harm is not the inconvenience; it is that a user who hits a false positive learns to route around the guard, which is the behaviour the guard exists to prevent.

items.title: One command runner, one closing-problems aggregator, one path classifier
acceptance: src/run.ts exports runCommand(cmd, {cwd, timeoutMs, output}) returning {code, signal, timedOut, tail}; output goes through a temp-file fd so grandchildren cannot block it, and a timeout test proves it returns
runVerification in src/gate.ts runs on runCommand with output inherited, and every existing gate --full test passes unedited
headSha and defaultBranch live in src/git.ts and src/worktree.ts no longer imports src/gate.ts

closingProblems(store, state, item) lives in a module that does not import gate.ts; the gate calls it for the active item and state set --status done refuses on any problem it returns, overridable only by --force --closed-by; the verification receipt check is its first member
src/pathclass.ts classifies a repo-relative path as test, doc or code with a hand-written ** and * matcher (no path.matchesGlob), covered by a table test

items.title: Tokens per item, per role and per model, recorded without slowing a hook
acceptance: Before building: a rung-4 note in the impl report answers whether cost-state is written before or after SessionEnd, whether it includes subagents, what --resume does to the transcript, and where /compact usage appears
.mstack/costs.tsv (committed) holds ts run target role agent_id model input cache_write cache_read output messages cost_usd source, one row per model, with (none) as the no-item sentinel

SessionStart and Stop write marks under git rev-parse --git-path mstack/, Stop only when the active item changed; a flush at SessionEnd, at SessionStart for leftover runs and inside mstack cost dedupes usage by message.id, skips isSidechain, scans the session's subagents and appends only the delta per key, so flushing twice changes nothing
When a cost-state line exists, a role=unattributed source=cost-state row per model reconciles the transcript sum to it
SubagentStop requires a report modified after the agent transcript's first timestamp, so a later-round subagent that writes nothing is caught

mstack cost [slug] [--by role|item|model] [--json] prints tokens, review rounds via roundOf and verifier-failed rows; rules.record_costs false turns recording off; .mstack/.gitattributes sets merge=union on costs.tsv, ledger.tsv and decisions.tsv
Hook paths stay within budget on a 50 MB synthetic transcript and a throwing parser never changes another hook's output

items.title: A sandbox benchmark that compares plain Claude Code, mstack before and mstack after on hidden tests
acceptance: A rung-4 spike note shows /mstack invoked from claude -p, the fields of the -p JSON result, that the plain arm does not load the installed mstack plugin, and how the PreToolUse guard behaves under bypassPermissions

sandbox/bench (gitignored, never pushed) holds a Python stdlib project whose visible tests pass, and six tasks, each an issue prompt plus hidden tests where every hidden test traces to a sentence of the issue

sandbox/bench/run.mjs runs arm x task x repetition in a fresh copy and appends hidden-test pass ratio, visible regressions, tokens, cost, turns and wall time to sandbox/bench/results/*.tsv; arms are plain, mstack-before (git archive of main when this item starts) and mstack-after (the checkout)

The baseline (plain and mstack-before on all six tasks, repetitions chosen from the spike's measured cost and recorded with mstack decide) is summarised in the impl report, with a stop-or-continue checkpoint recorded with mstack decide
every arm runs with --permission-mode auto and no allowlist, so one classifier applies to all arms alike
items.decision_required: Which repositories and which bug-fix commits make the pilot's three tasks? The answer decides the languages, the test commands and the budget cap per run.

The router, review and design skills say what is now true about cross-model second opinions, and docs/wiki/The-Agents.md shows each agent's model
A live subagent transcript shows message.model sonnet for the implementer and opus for the reviewer, pasted in the impl report

items.title: Items carry a size and the commit they started from
acceptance: size s|m|l is accepted by state add and state set, clearable (absent means m), and an invalid value is refused rather than dropped

The gate fails an item with base and size s whose code diff from base exceeds 60 lines or 3 files, and sdd with size s is refused

items.title: The gate reads the requirement-to-test table instead of trusting it
acceptance: src/rtable.ts parses the last | R | Test | Where | table of the highest-round impl report, splitting cells on unescaped pipes outside backticks

For the active item with base, from reviewing and at the done transition, every acceptance index A<n> or spec R<n> has a row, and every Where cites existing test-classified files at in-range lines or says n/a: with a reason of at least 12 characters
Closed items and items without base are never checked, and the implementer prose defines the one table header

items.title: mstack verify --mutation proves the tests fail without the change
acceptance: verify --mutation reverts the code part of base..HEAD in place (store, tests and docs excluded), confirms a green baseline first, runs the obligations and records mutation-killed, mutation-survived or mutation-blocked in verification.tsv keyed by code tree

A lock under the git dir holds the restore list; restore runs in finally and on SIGINT/SIGTERM, the tree is clean afterwards, verify --restore repairs a SIGKILLed run, PreToolUse denies git commit/add/stash while the lock exists, and the gate fails on a lock
From verifying, an item with base, size other than s and a code diff needs a killed receipt at the current code tree, enforced in the gate and at the done transition

items.title: Review rounds, report sizes and spec sizes have a budget
acceptance: decisions.tsv gains a trailing item column; fanout plan --kind review --solo allocates review_<slug>_r<N>.md, requires --justify from round 3 and writes the review-r<N> decision row, and prints the last reviewed sha that is still an ancestor of HEAD
The gate fails the active item with base when a round-3-or-later review report has no matching decision row, or when any of its reports exceeds 24 KB
Implementer rounds after the first write impl_<slug>_r<N>.md deltas carrying the full R-to-test table
specifying to spec_ready is refused when spec.md declares more requirements than its size allows (m 12, l 30) unless forced with a decision row

items.title: The ceremony scales with the item's size
acceptance: The router, the feature and bug-fix playbooks and the design, review and implement skills carry one matrix: s skips design candidates and the panel, m adds mutation, l adds understand, design twice and a lens panel; delegation and an independent review hold at every size
The router assigns a size at intake, and the gate fails an l item at verifying with no review round of two or more lens reports

items.description: Reproduced at rung 4: rows 70 (implementer test-verified) and 71 (reviewer verifier-failed) at a4e6c784; './bin/mstack ledger check benchmark-harness' prints 'PASS test-verified at a4e6c784 by implementer', exit 0. check() keeps the best row by rank, so the implementer's self-assessment hides the independent rejection. items.title: A hard benchmark tier where plain Claude Code does not solve every task
acceptance: 3-4 tasks on a larger template (at least ~2k lines, more than one plausible place to fix), written as symptoms a user would report, with hidden tests for the reported behaviour plus regression tests on existing documented behaviour, and at least one trap where the obvious fix breaks something else
every hidden test traces to the issue or to behaviour the template's README or visible tests already document; reference patches pass them and the pristine template fails them

a calibration run shows whether plain solves every hard task across at least two repetitions; if it does, the tier is made harder once and recalibrated, and if plain still solves every task the user decides how the tier is used (decision row)
the hard-tier baseline (plain and mstack-before, repetitions recorded with mstack decide) is summarised with solved rate first, then cost

items.title: Benchmark hygiene follow-ups from the item 48 review, before the item 45 rerun

DESIGN.md states the widened leak rule: committed text names no hidden values, assertions, patch contents, nor which side or fix is correct; and states that self-checks are not run while a batch is running
